_meta.indication: LAZCLUZE is indicated in combination with amivantamab for the first-line treatment of adult patients with locally advanced or metastatic NSCLC with EGFR exon 19 deletions or exon 21 L858R substitution mutations, as detected by an FDA-approved test.

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized 2:2:1 to open-label amivantamab plus lazertinib (Arm A), double-blind osimertinib plus matching oral placebo (Arm B, control), or double-blind lazertinib plus oral matching placebo (Arm C); no crossover after progression; stratified by EGFR mutation type, Asian race, and presence of brain metastases.
pivotal_trials.population: Adult patients with previously untreated locally advanced unresectable or metastatic NSCLC harboring EGFR exon 19 deletions or exon 21 L858R substitution mutations.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Progression-free survival (PFS) assessed by blinded independent central review (BICR) for Arm A compared to Arm B; overall survival was a key secondary endpoint.
pivotal_trials.n: N=1,074 total randomized: Arm A (amivantamab + lazertinib) n=429, Arm B (osimertinib) n=429, Arm C (lazertinib) n=217.
pivotal_trials.result: Met primary endpoint: PFS HR 0.70 (95% CI 0.58, 0.85; p=0.0002) favoring Arm A; median PFS 23.7 months (95% CI 19.1, 27.7) in Arm A vs 16.6 months (95% CI 14.8, 18.5) in Arm B. First interim OS HR 0.81 (95% CI 0.62, 1.06; p=0.120), not statistically significant.

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (>=20%) were rash, nail toxicity, infusion-related reaction (amivantamab), musculoskeletal pain, edema, stomatitis, VTE, paresthesia, fatigue, diarrhea, constipation, COVID-19, hemorrhage, dry skin, decreased appetite, pruritus, nausea, and ocular toxicity. Rash occurred in 86% (Grade 3 or 4 26%) and nail toxicity in 71% (11%). Serious adverse reactions occurred in 49% of patients; fatal adverse reactions in 7%. VTE occurred in 36% of patients (Grade 3 in 10%).
target_moa: Lazertinib is an oral third-generation tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI) of EGFR, with activity in NSCLC harboring EGFR exon 19 deletions and exon 21 L858R substitution mutations as well as exon 20 T790M mutations; given with amivantamab, a bispecific antibody binding EGFR and the MET receptor.
companion_dx_detail: cobas EGFR Mutation Test v2 used to detect EGFR exon 19 deletions or exon 21 L858R substitution mutations in tumor or plasma specimens.

advisory_committee.vote: FDA did not refer this application to an advisory committee meeting because it did not raise significant public health questions.

description.text: Updated labeling with final overall survival analysis from the MARIPOSA trial, fulfilling postmarketing commitment 4681-2

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental new drug application provides for updated final overall survival analysis, in fulfillment of the August 19, 2024, Post-Marketing Commitment 4681-2, based on results from the MARIPOSA trial.

basis.text: The application was designated Priority Review.

summary.text: This original NDA received Priority Review and was granted traditional (full) approval based on the randomized MARIPOSA trial, which met its primary PFS endpoint; the application was not referred to an advisory committee.

citations.quote: The results of MARIPOSA, a large, multiregional, randomized controlled trial, demonstrate substantial evidence of effectiveness and meet the statutory evidentiary standard for traditional approval for the use of amivantamab in combination with lazertinib as first-line therapy for patients with locally advanced or metastatic NSCLC harboring *EGFR* exon 19 deletions or exon 21 L858R substitution mut

The FDA did not refer this application to an advisory committee meeting because the application did not raise significant public health questions regarding the role of lazertinib in combination with amivantamab in the intended patient population that would benefit from an external committee of experts.

requirement.text: 4681-1 Conduct comprehensive safety analyses from clinical studies that further characterize the known serious risk of venous thromboembolic events (VTEs) in patients treated with amivantamab intravenously (IV) and patients treated with amivantamab subcutaneously (SC), in combination with lazertinib. Provide the incidence, timing, and outcome of VTEs by grade in patients who did not receive prophylactic anticoagulation, who received prophylactic anticoagulation for the initial 4 months of study therapy only, who continued prophylactic anticoagulation beyond 4 months of study therapy, and who required initiation of treatment-level anticoagulation. Monitor patients for VTEs throughout study therapy until treatment discontinuation.
